summary: Read-only forensic investigation of six production complaints about the QA agent: two were confirmed P0 security/execution-trust issues (any logged-in user can see everyone's runs; every scheduled BrowserStack run fails on invalid credentials), plus confirmed browser-kill and interrupted-state explainability defects. Evidence was gathered with controlled probes on the live store, and no production behavior was changed.
what_was_done: Verified the cross-user visibility complaint: mission, session, finding and evidence records carry no owner identity, and every read endpoint returns the whole workspace to any authenticated caller — anyone can open another user's run, report and live session stream

Traced the 'runs freeze' complaint to four independent causes, the main one being that starting a new mission's turn closes the browser of any run currently waiting at a question, so when it resumes the browser panel is permanently stuck while activity continues

Verified the 'unexpected INTERRUPTED' complaint on a live session: a server restart immediately after the agent asked a question flipped the session to interrupted with its pending question dropped and no reason exposed by the API

Proved the scheduler itself works — all 11 daily schedules fired, plus a controlled every-minute schedule — while discovering that every scheduled run fails at browser launch because BrowserStack is enabled with invalid credentials and strict mode correctly refuses local fallback

Traced the evidence-collection opacity and 'No browser yet' panel complaints to their exact code paths, and classified the meeting-audio failures as an environment limitation (no audio device in the container, no fake-device launch flags)
Produced an ordered minimal-fix action list that the P0 fix pack (tickets #9035–#9041) now implements
what_was_tested: Anonymous and authenticated API reads against the live server confirming the isolation gap
Controlled probe schedule (every minute) proving the scheduler fires, persists its run, and rolls nextRun
Store inspection: 51,262 evidence nodes, 2,833 never-started mission shells, 109 interrupted missions, live interrupted session specimen 396edfcf
Runtime profiling: Node 292MB RSS at 0.7% CPU, all API latencies under 175ms — backend not the freeze bottleneck
